newsitem.title: USA: National carlot beef trade weekly review - USDA.
newsitem.headline: National carlot beef trade weekly review - USDA.

text.p: Boxed beef trading was rather lethargic for the week, demand was very light, and the offerings were moderate to heavy, consequently the boxed beef items traded lower, and live cattle costs were higher.

Retail and HRI demand remaind light for immediate and forward needs. Rib and loin cuts were under the most downward pressure and traded lower. Chuck cuts started the week steady, but by mid week processors cut prices sharply lower.
Round cuts had moderate demand for the week and traded generally steady early, but some weakness develop late in the trading period on some inside round cuts.

Closely trimmed items followed somewhat the same market trends, demand was slow and these items traded lower. Beef trimmings traded lower on mostly moderate demand and offerings were generally moderate to heavy for post holiday needs.
Fed cattle and blended coarse ground items were uneven, the Fed cattle grinds were lower and blended coarse ground items were higher on light to moderate demand and offerings.

The Estimated Composite of Boxed Beef Cutout values of Choice 1-3 550/700 carcasses Dn 1.93 at 103.46; 700/850 Dn 2.34 at 101.44; Select 1-3 550/700 carcasses Dn 1.40 at 99.46; 700/850 Dn 1.54 at 97.75.

For the week select and choice rib primal 3.00 to 4.00 lower; Select and Choice chuck primal 1.00 to 1.50 lower; Select and Choice round primal steady to 1.00 lower; Select and Choice loin primal 2.00 to 5.00 lower; Closely trimmed items 1.50 to 2.50 lower; Beef trimmings 4.00 lower; Fed cattle grinds 5.00 to 6.00 lower and blended coarse ground items 2.00 to 3.00 higher.
The boneless beef market was pressured sharply lower this week. Increased availability of slaughter cows in many areas and light demand going into the holiday shortened week forced prices lower.

Cow carcasses finished the week lower in response to the decline in boneless beef and softening of the cow cuts markets. Most of the Utility cuts were steady to weak, but Cutter cuts were mostly weak with the tenderloins experiencing the most decline and traded lower on very light demand.

Utility carcasses mostly 1.00 higher; Cutter 1.00-2.00 lower. Fresh 90% boneless beef 4.00-4.50 lower; 85% 1.50-2.50 lower; 75% 1.50-4.50 lower; 65% 1.00-2.00 lower. The Cutter cow carcass gross cut-out value for Thursday, August 29, 1996 was estimated at 69.74 per cwt., down 2.72 from a week ago Friday.
